items.title: Hyderabad: Seven EFLU students from ABVP arrested for alleged attack on NSUI members
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A dispute between members of the right-wing student organisation Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), and Congress’ student wing National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) escalated into violence at the English and Foreign Languages University (EFLU) in Hyderabad. NSUI members have alleged that a group of ABVP cadres attacked them with iron rods, bamboo sticks, beer bottles, and belts in one of the men’s hostels, and used abusive casteist slurs, in the early hours of August 14. Complaints were lodged by both sides at the Osmania University police, who said that a total of 14 men were taken into custody from both sides over the violence. Of them, seven ABVP members were sent to judicial custody. According to the complaint filed by NSUI member Nikhil Kumar (18), a second-year BA French student, the violence was triggered by an incident during a students’ protest at the Mahlaq Bai Chanda Hostel for Women around 10.30 pm on August 13. There, Nikhil alleged that the accused Viswajeet Singh, Pranav Pathak, Rishabh Singh, Rudra, and other ABVP cadres used casteist slurs to abuse his friend, Rishit Naik, and physically assaulted another NSUI member, Sonu Raj. The NSUI members went to the OU police station to file a complaint over this incident, according to Nikhil. Later, around 4 am, he alleged that the accused ABVP members entered his room in Basheer Hostel for Men. They were allegedly carrying iron rods, bamboo sticks, beer bottles, belts etc. and attacked the NSUI members with these weapons. The complaint alleged that a student named Harsh Tambrakar was beaten with a beer bottle on his head and neck, resulting in heavy bleeding. The accused allegedly beat another student, Sohil Yadav, with an iron rod and broke a mirror on his face. Another student, Prashanth Singh, was also beaten with bamboo sticks, it said, for filing a complaint against them. The complaint alleged that the accused threatened the students not to work with NSUI, and used vulgar language to speak about their women friends. The ABVP members also filed a complaint alleging that it was the rival group that attacked them first. The complaint by a student named Rishabh Kumar alleged that a group of more than 20 people entered his room and beat him with a belt and an iron rod, threatening him to leave the campus. items.title: ‘Go to Pakistan’: Kerala school owner faces protest over remarks to students
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The owner of a private school in Kerala sent a message to a parents’ WhatsApp group telling students who missed the Independence Day celebrations to “go to Pakistan” and saying they did not deserve to live in India. Raju Davis, the owner of Dr Raju Davis International and Sainik School in Mala, Thrissur, sparked outrage with his comments. The voice message was reportedly sent after the Independence Day celebration. “This is a really bad thing, and it's unbearable. When celebrating a country's Independence Day, staying at home in defiance of it is very wrong. Such people should go and live in some other country like Pakistan. They do not deserve to live here,” he said in the voice note. He also warned that students who failed to attend the celebrations would be barred from entering their classrooms and would have to provide a formal explanation. “I won't allow them in my class tomorrow unless the parents come directly and give me an explanation,” he said. He also says that such behaviour is among the reasons children grow up to be disrespectful. The Student Federation of India (SFI) conducted a protest march to the school after his remarks became public. Despite the criticism, Raju defended his remarks, stating in a clarification that he stood by his comments. “I never mentioned any religion. I didn’t say go to Bangladesh, Arab countries or Sudan. I said Pakistan because of my patriotism. Because Pakistan is an enemy country for India. I am not thinking it's wrong, because I never made any communal remarks,” he told Media One. He then clarified that the students would be barred from attending only one class period. “During this single period, the school will conduct a lesson on Indian independence, as the students missed Independence Day,” he said. Meanwhile, Fayis AH, president of the Fraternity Movement in Thrissur district, has filed a police complaint against Raju in Thrissur.
